I check that case and if the possibility is really there, I send a request for payment to the insurant and make me a reminder.

When we receive the money, I make a booking and close the case.

If he is right, I simply close the case.
If he is wrong, I forward the case to a collection agency.
It the deadline for disagreement is reached and we haven't received any money, I forward the case to the collection agency as well.

result.process_description:
If an insurant could be possibly subrogated against, I get information about that. 
I check that case and if the possibility is really there, I send a request for payment to the insurant and make me a reminder. 
If recourse is not possible, I close the case. 
When we receive the money, I make a booking and close the case. 
If the insurant disagrees with the recourse, I'll have to check the reasoning of that. 
If he is right, I simply close the case. 
If he is wrong, I forward the case to a collection agency. It the deadline for disagreement is reached and we haven't received any money, I forward the case to the collection agency as well.

Use sequence flows inside one participant process and message flows between different participants. Never use sequence flow across pools.

result.rule: When the description focuses on one participant’s workflow and mentions an outside party only as the recipient or source of requests, payments, or responses, without describing that party’s own process: Model the described workflow within its participant pool; do not add a separate pool or message flows solely to represent those mentions. Represent relevant receipt or decision points within the described process.

When the description identifies work performed by a participant as the first step of the process: Model that work as an activity after a start event and before the subsequent activity; do not represent the work itself as the start event.

When the description assigns activities in one organizational process to multiple internal roles: Represent the organization’s process in one participant pool and use lanes for the stated internal roles; do not omit the process pool or model ordinary internal roles as separate pools.

When the description attributes an action that prompts further work to a specific actor: Label the corresponding activity with that actor performing the stated action, rather than recasting it from the perspective of another participant receiving or handling it.
